newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault unions call one-hour strike over job losses.
newsitem.headline: Renault unions call one-hour strike over job losses.

text.p: Labour unions at beleaguered French carmaker Renault SA called Monday for a one-hour strike at all its factories in France, Belgium and Spain amid reports that the company will announce major job cuts.

Renault said chairman Louis Schweitzer would this week meet representatives of a Belgian assembly plant slated to be closed but declined comment on reports that 3,000 jobs in France also will be eliminated.

The Belgian government and the northern Flanders region also said they would sue Renault over procedural issues after European Commissioner Karel Van Miert said the group had not followed European directive on consulting unions.
Eight unions from Belgium, France and Spain called the one-hour strike and said they planned to take legal steps to thwart the decision to close the Belgain Vilvoorde plant.
A Renault spokeswoman said Schweitzer had agreed to meet staff this week at the Belgian plant, where 3,100 jobs will be eliminated, but the time and place had not been set.
On Thursday he will attend a works council meeting in Paris to face angry French workers who fear job cuts on top of the Belgian closure.

"The big problem in the auto sector is overcapacity, a problem which no-one has dared to touch for 20 years for obvious labour reasons," said a broker. "The fact that Renault is tackling it is a good sign."
Renault shed 1,641 jobs last year and 1,735 in 1995.
